newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude down, Oman weakens, Tapis done at +40.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude down, Oman weakens, Tapis done at +40.

text.p: Trading on the Middle East crude market was still fairly slow, keeping traders uncertain of the direction of prices following the release of official prices.
But Oman trades heard done recently were at deeper discounts than deals done before the release of the official MPM price, which traders saw as a reflection of weak July demand.
A major was heard to have bought an Oman cargo at MPM -18 cents per barrel from a shosha.
Another major was also heard to have bought 200kb of July Oman from another shosha at MPM -20.
Last week, Oman traded at MPM -12 and at MPM -15.
Only one trade for Abu Dhabi crude was heard, a 600,000 barrel cargo of Murban that a European major sold to Kenya, at ADNOC +70 c+f.
With a freight rate of 90 cents per barrel, this would netback around to ADNOC -20/25, said the seller.
Following this trade, just two cargoes of Murban were on offer in the July market, traders said.
In Asian crudes, Bangchak bought a 600,000-barrel cargo of July Tapis at just less than APPI +40, a refinery source confirmed.
The purchase was extra to two million barrels of Oman and 500,000 barrels of Murban that the refinery had bought earlier.

The large volume was due to a tightness in the refinery's term supplies for July, as most of its term contracts were for quarters, and there were more liftings in August than in July, the source said.
There were also rumours of a July Miri sold by a western trader at OSP -15, but the deal could not be confirmed.
A July parcel of Bach Ho was heard traded between Japanese at OSP +45.
